questions.q: A Technical Architect is deciding between a criteria-based sharing rule and Apex managed sharing for a new requirement. Which situation specifically calls for Apex managed sharing?
options: The grant depends on a calculation across related records that the sharing-rule criteria UI cannot express
Sharing a record with everyone in a public group whenever a single picklist field equals a fixed value
Sharing needs to apply only to the record owner's own records
The org-wide default is already Public Read/Write on the object
questions.explain: Sharing rules can only express conditions available in their criteria UI (field values, owner role/group). Logic that requires traversing related records or external calculations must be implemented in Apex.

questions.q: What does the RowCause field on a share object record identify?
options: The access level granted (Read, Edit, or All)
The user or group receiving access
Whether the share row will survive an owner change
The reason the share row exists — owner, manual, a sharing rule, or a custom Apex sharing reason
questions.explain: RowCause records why a share row exists. Apex managed sharing is specifically share rows created under a custom Apex-defined RowCause.

questions.q: A custom object's org-wide default is already Public Read/Write. What happens if Apex code inserts a __Share row granting Read access on a record of that object?
options: The insert throws a DuplicateRowError immediately
It silently upgrades the org-wide default to Public Read/Write for all records
It succeeds but has no practical effect, since everyone already has that access implicitly via OWD
It is rejected because Apex managed sharing requires Modify All Data on the running user
questions.explain: A share row can never grant less than, or redundant access relative to, what OWD already provides — if OWD already grants that level org-wide, the extra share row is a no-op.

questions.q: A record with a manual share and a record with an Apex managed share (custom RowCause) both have their owner reassigned. What happens to each share row?
options: Both are deleted automatically on reassignment
The manual share is deleted automatically; the Apex managed share persists until code removes it
Both persist unchanged after reassignment
The Apex managed share is deleted automatically; the manual share persists until a user removes it
questions.explain: Manual sharing is cleared automatically on an ownership change. Apex managed sharing is not — it persists until the governing code explicitly deletes it, which is why it suits durable, code-owned business facts.

questions.q: Why should sharing-logic Apex that inserts share rows for multiple records use Database.insert(records, false) with SaveResult inspection instead of a plain allOrNothing insert?
options: Because a DuplicateRowError on one record would otherwise roll back the entire batch instead of allowing partial success
Because share objects cannot be inserted with DML at all, only via SOQL
Because AccessLevel values must be validated client-side before insert
Because RowCause values are read-only after the first insert
questions.explain: If a user/group already holds an equal-or-greater grant under a different cause, the insert for that row throws a DuplicateRowError. Using the partial-success form with SaveResult inspection lets the rest of the batch succeed.
